tossups.text: Muhammad II of Khwarezmia had a messenger sent by this man beheaded. Merkits kidnapped this man's wife Börte, and he employed the general Subotai. After this man's death, his son Tolui served as regent until the succession of Ögedei. This man's birth name was Temujin, and his descendants include Jochi, Chagatai, and Kublai. For 10 points, name this conqueror, the first Khan of the Mongol empire.

In his sixth meditation, Descartes ("Day-cart") explains how this concept proves the existence of an external world. The Cartesian conception of this concept is contrasted with his rationalist successor Spinoza's idea of this concept, with Spinoza believing that this concept represents a singular infinite substance through which all of reality flows. Fideism is the position that belief in this concept should exist independent of reason. Leibniz's optimism offers an answer to the question about this concept being good, just, and all-powerful despite the existence of evil. For 10 points, name this concept that Anselm claimed to prove with his ontological argument.

The 1989 restoration of a painting by this artist prompted the formation of the APIAH, who objected to the removal of a reddish-brown hue from a now-green tabard coat. A large dagger and a statue of a sphinx are concealed by the dress of a woman who reaches toward a white-clad Hercules in this artist's Allegory of Virtue and Vice. A string quartet gathers around an hourglass in a painting by this man that was cut in half by Napoleon's troops and transferred to the Louvre, where it is now the largest painting. The presence of slaves, jesters, and drunken German soldiers in another of this man's paintings drew the attention of the Inquisition, prompting him to change its title from The Last Supper. For 10 points, name this Venetian painter of The Wedding at Cana and The Feast in the House of Levi.

A female corpse dragged out of this river is the basis for the face on most CPR dummies. An island in this river whose name translates to "Island of the Swans" contains a 37-foot replica of the Statue of Liberty. The Rouen Cathedral overlooks this river. This river separates twenty arrondissements into banks known as the "Gauche" ("gohsh") and "Droite ("dwat") ." This river passes through the wine-making region of Burgundy near Dijon before flowing into the English Channel near Le Havre. The Île de la Cité in this river is spanned by the Pont Neuf bridge and is the location of the Notre-Dame cathedral. For 10 points, name this river in Paris.

They can be directly coupled to alkyl, vinyl, or aryl halides by using a nickel catalyst in the Kumada reaction, and when added to triethyl orthoformate, they form aldehydes in the Bodroux-Chichibabin synthesis. Solutions of them spontaneously dimerize via the Schlenk equilibrium, which is why it is necessary for them to be coordinated to aprotic solvents like diethyl ether or THF. More common reactions of them are addition to a nitrile to form an imine, and the formation of tertiary alcohols by adding them to an ester. However, they most famously add to carbonyl compounds to create alcohols, and since they are strong bases, adding water creates the corresponding alkane. For 10 points, what are these magnesium halide organometallic reagents, named for their French discoverer?

In the mid-18th century, a Dr. Brownrigg from North Carolina proposed that the American colonies could use this crop to replace imports of olive oil, a suggestion that was not taken up. Samuel Crocker Cobb was an important trader in this crop in the late 19th century, whose diaries detail an unpredictable trade in this crop with Gorée. Sacks of this crop were piled into massive pyramids by traders such as the one-time richest man in West Africa, Alhassan Dantata. Frank Samuel led a project centered on this crop that exemplifies a "second colonial occupation" outlined by Anthony Low and John Lonsdale. Following its introduction, this crop superseded a similar plant commonly named for the (*) Bambara people in importance in West Africa. The Spanish word for this crop comes from the Nahuatl word tlācacahuatl [tlah-cah-CAH-wattle]. Converted Sherman tanks called "shervicks" were utilized in a failed attempt to industrially produce this crop in British Tanzania. For 10 points, what is this legume that comes in Virginia and Valencia varieties and is commonly boiled in the South?

This man's work Psychological Types provided the basis for the Myers-Briggs Test, which built on his ideas of introverts and extroverts. He proposed that all of mankind shares a body of indirect knowledge, and posited the shadow, persona, self, anima, and animus as the five main archetypes, For 10 points, name this Swiss founder of analytic psychology who developed the idea of the collective unconscious.

Imaging is limited by this phenomenon, as described by the equation angular resolution equals 1.22 times lambda over D; that is the Rayleigh criterion. The equation two times distance times the sine of the scattering angle equals n times the wavelength describes the scattering from a crystal due to this phenomenon in Bragg's Law. Thomas Young demonstrated the interference caused by this phenomenon in his double-slit experiment. For 10 points, name this phenomenon in which light bends around an obstacle.

Three of these beings legendarily divided an inheritance by stuffing gold in their mouths. The ancestor of these mythical figures was born from venom from Elivagar and drank from the milk of Auoumbla. Loki turned the goddess of youth into a nut after she was kidnapped by another of these beings, and the goddess of skiing, Skadi, is also one of these figures. Bestla, the mother of Odin, was one of these figures, and the earth, ocean, humans, and dwarves were all formed from parts of one of these figures. For 10 points, name these beings that include Thiazi and Ymir, who may not actually be unusually large.

This author compared the moon to "a fragment of angry candy" in "the Cambridge ladies who live in furnished souls". This author mentions "bayonets roasted hot with heat" in a poem about a "conscientious object-or". This author of "i sing of Olaf glad and big" wrote a poem referring to "sun moon stars rain" and "women and men (both ding and dong)". For 10 points, name this poet of "anyone lived in a pretty how town" who notably avoided capital letters.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for atp and muscle energy. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this contraction-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The contraction is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in atp and muscle energy.

tossups.text: After learning of Christine Stuart's engagement, this woman accepts the proposal of her classmate at Queen's College, where she studies to be a teacher in Avonlea. This woman becomes close friends with Diana Barry, and marries Gilbert Blythe after she goes to live with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert on Prince Edward Island. For ten points, name this orphan who lives at Green Gables.

Along with objects relating to Christ's passion, rings of figures hold these objects while circling around a glowing Madonna and Child in The Glorification of the Virgin by Geertgen tot Sint Jans. Naked figures hold hands in a ring around one of these objects on a red tent on a cylindrical wooden house in a Last Judgement in Bruges. In another painting, a man standing on one of these objects bends over to balance a large (+) egg on his back. In that painting, a large, pink one of these objects rests on a white disk atop a head glancing sideways. These objects feature in a section of that painting just below the 'Tree Man,' to the left of a bird-like demon eating a sinner, above a section for gamblers. For 10 points, name these objects featured in a section of Hell in The Garden of Earthly Delights.
acceptableAnswers: specific kinds of instruments like lutes

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for limbic system. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cerebrum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cerebrum is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in limbic system.

tossups.text: This organ is separated into right and left halves by the angular incisure, below which lies its antrum, where G cells and D cells are located. One part of this organ features glands that form polyps in Cowden's syndrome, and "magic looping" takes place under parasympathetic control in that same part, its fundus, where gases can accumulate. Folds in the walls of this organ are called rugae, and its chief cells secrete pepsinogen. This organ's contents are prevented from flowing into the next by the pyloric sphincter; those contents are often called chyme. Hormones characteristic of this organ include gastrin, and its interior is maintained at pH as low as four. For 10 points, name this digestive system component between the esophagus and small intestine.

This thinker's taped conversations with James Baldwin were the basis for A Rap on Race. This thinker examined Chambri female dominance in Papua New Guinea in Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies. This thinker's "fateful hoaxing" titles a 1999 book by Derek Freeman, which discusses her examination of adolescent sexuality on the island of Ta'u in Polynesia. For 10 points, name this American anthropologist who wrote Coming of Age in Samoa.

The delta form of this substance is bound to albumin. Diazosulfanilic acid reacts with this substance in the van den Bergh reaction. Excess levels of a form of it may cross the blood-brain barrier and cause kernicterus. The star-28 allele of UGT1A1 can cause high levels of this compound to circulate in the blood in Gilbert's syndrome. The Z,Z form of this compound is converted into the more soluble E,Z-isomer during phototherapy on newborns. This open-chain tetrapyrrole is solubilized by glucuronyltransferase, and increased amounts of it are released in hemolytic anemia. It is metabolized from a "verdin" precursor and broken down to the compounds that give feces and urine their colors. For 10 points, name this product of heme catabolism that at high levels causes jaundice.

"All the world is a joke" are the words to the one that closes Verdi's Falstaff, and the first movement of Beethoven's string quartet opus 131 is this type of piece. Brahms wrote a set of variations and one of these based on a theme by Handel, and twelve of these pieces are separated by eleven interludes in Paul Hindemith's Ludus tonalis. The "Of Science" section of Richard Strauss's Also Sprach Zarathustra is one of these employing all twelve notes of the chromatic scale. One element of this type of piece can be real or tonal; that is the answer, which is a repetition of the subject in a different voice. For 10 points, identify this type of composition paired with preludes in The Well-Tempered Clavier by Bach, who also wrote a piece called The Art of them.

Double or triple bonds are superseded by two or three single bonds. Substituents are ranked by decreasing atomic number. Two groups with the same rank are separated by their first point of difference. Thus 1-methylethyl ranks higher than ethyl ranks higher than methyl. Place the lowest priority group furthest away. If the remaining groups are arranged counterclockwise, the stereocenter is S; if clockwise then R. Not always in agreement with the sign of specific rotation, for ten points name these rules invented by a trio of chemist to designate handedness of molecules.

In this play, Lennox and a nobleman from Fife enter Inverness Castle, breaking the protagonist's focus on a murder. This play's title murderer becomes the Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, in accordance with a prophecy given by three witches to him and Banquo, and takes the throne after killing King Duncan. For ten points, name this "Scottish play" by William Shakespeare.

parts.text: Name this general, who led the Redshirts in Expedition of the Thousand to defeat the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

Garibaldi was prominent during the unification of this country, also known as the Risorgimento. The Carbonari were another group prominent during this country's unification, which led to Victor Emmanuel II ruling from Rome.
This other Italian led a famous "March on Rome" which established his fascist party's power. This dictator known as "Il Duce" was in power for much of World War II.

bonuses.leadin: This leader was called the "Hero of Two Worlds" for his involvement in both European and South American conflicts. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This book, included among the minor prophets, is a fable built around a prophet who got caught in a massive storm while sailing to Tarshish.
Jonah was sent to preach to this last capital city of the Assyrian Empire.

Jonah's preaching of repentance to Nineveh contrasts with this minor prophet, who prophesied the destruction of Nineveh, and only the destruction of Nineveh, in the three chapters of his namesake book.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a book of the Bible, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this painter, who worked with his brother-in-law, Simone Martini, on an Annunciation including St. Margaret and St. Anansus.
Unless you believe Vasari, Martini was probably the pupil of this leading Sienese artist. His Maesta altarpiece was tragically sawn in half in 1711 and was originally painted for the Siena Cathedral.
Martini's saint-strewn Maesta takes up the entire north wall of the Great Council Hall of this Sienese town hall that also contains Lorenzetti's Allegory of Good and Bad Government.

bonuses.leadin: Dozens of people huddle under Mary's robes while angels stand behind her in this artist's Virgin of Mercy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The abundance of dead whales led European passersby to give this name to the Namibian coast north of the Swakop River.
The southwestern coastline of India, from Konkan southward, is given this name. It is west of the Western Ghats and borders the Arabian Sea.
This southern coast of France, containing Nice and Monaco, is known for its luxury yachts and popularity with the ultra-rich around the world.

bonuses.leadin: Name the following coasts, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these star shaped structures which extend from centrosomes at the poles of a dividing cell outwards towards the cell cortex, and are not to be confused with polar microtubules.
Asters help determine the plane of cleavage of during this final stage of mitosis, which follows telophase, and results in two identical daughter nuclei.
Experiments suggest that microtubules shorten at the kinetochore ends during this phase when chromosomes separate towards opposite poles of the cell

bonuses.leadin: The absence of them can cause a delay in spindle elongation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Mesoamerican site in the Yucatan that formed a namesake league of 16 city-states around 1280 AD under the Cocom family, which lasted until the revolt of the Xiu family.
The Southern Maya heartland contains potbelly architecture marked by large stone heads, similar to those of this much earlier civilization which had centers at La Venta and San Lorenzo.

In addition to using other material like flint and obsidian, Mayan aristocrats conducted human bloodletting rituals using the spine of this aquatic creature. It's depicted in a Yaxchilan relief where a man pierces his penis with one of these spines, while a woman jabs a thorny vine through her tongue.

bonuses.leadin: The ruler of this city, Hunac Ceel, supposedly convinced the ruler at Chichen Itza to steal the bride of Izamal, inciting a war that depopulated Chichen Itza. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this currency, now used by 17 nations including Spain, Italy, and Ireland.
This country, the largest economy in the European Union, previously used the Mark as its currency before switching to the Euro.
The Euro has been threatened by the potential default of this country on its debts. It replaced Prime Minister George Papandreo with Lucas Papademos in response to riots.

bonuses.leadin: This currency was established in 1992 by the Treaty of Maastricht. For 10 points each;

parts.text: Name this president who used the springs to find relief for his crippling disease while leading the United States through most of World War II.
Roosevelt suffered from this disease, caused by a virus that makes muscles weak.
Roosevelt was elected to this many terms as president, the most that any president has ever been elected to in American history.

bonuses.leadin: This man spent some time in Warm Springs, Georgia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Norse god of war, the son of Odin and Frigg.
Tyr's hand was eaten by this wolf-giant-thing, the son of Loki, in order to construct a magical chain to bind him.
At Ragnarok, Tyr is destined to fight this watchdog of the underworld that guards Helheim. This creature is known for his four eyes and blood-drenched chest.

bonuses.leadin: This god is identified with the Tiwaz rune. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author of As I Lay Dying, who wrote another novel that follows the Compson family called The Sound and the Fury.

William Faulkner was a leading figure of a "Gothic" movement named after this broad region in the United States, which is composed of states like Mississippi and Virginia, who seceded in the American Civil War.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on the Confederacy by asking “what general region did the Confederacy encompass?”

parts.text: Another Southern Gothic author was Flannery O'Connor, who wrote this short story where the Grandmother encounters The Misfit while on a road trip.
parts.answer: Good Man Is Hard to Find
acceptableAnswers: Good Man Is Hard to Find
The Good Man Is Hard to Find

bonuses.leadin: A novel by this author follows the Bundren family as they go to bury their matriarch Addie. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with defecation reflex.
What is the main function of the colon in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to defecation reflex.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this literary "generation" that included Jack Kerouac and the author of the poem "Howl," Allen Ginsberg.
Ginsberg's "A Supermarket in California" mentions seeing this poet "eyeing the grocery boys." This poet wrote "I Sing the Body Electric", "Crossing Brooklyn Ferry", and "O Captain! My Captain!".
Whitman's "O Captain! My Captain!" was an elegy to this president who led the U.S. through the Civil War.

bonuses.leadin: This literary movement's works include William S. Burroughs's Naked Lunch. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this composer whose Cello Concerto in B minor was premiered in 1895 by Leo Stern.
Inspired by Native American and African-American musical traditions, this Dvořák symphony introduces the main theme of its Largo second movement with a solo for the English horn.

Describe the rhythm of the first three notes of that English horn solo in terms of "LONG" and "short" notes. For example, the words "Let it be" follow a "short, short, LONG" rhythm in the Beatles song.

bonuses.leadin: This composer was inspired by folk music to write pieces such as the Dumky Trio and the American String Quartet. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with muscle fatigue.
What is the main function of the contraction in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to muscle fatigue.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Give this property that a matrix defining a quadratic form must have in order to define an inner product. A matrix has this property if and only if it can be written as a matrix B times the conjugate transpose of B.

One way to find such a matrix B is to employ this factorization, which is unique for a positive definite matrix. Using this decomposition is more eficient than the LU factorization to solve a linear system for definite matrices.

The output of the Cholesky decomposition has this additional property that all numbers above the diagonal are zero. This property is named for the shape formed by the non-zero numbers in such a matrix.

bonuses.leadin: Unlike local maxima or saddles, local minima have Hessian matrices with this property. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this founder of psychoanalysis who described wish fulfillment in The Interpretation of Dreams.
Freud's book Beyond the Pleasure Principle discusses this adaptive element of the human mind holding us back from primal urges. It is often grouped with the ego and id.
Freud wrote about this entity "and its discontents" in another work. He asserted that it formulates laws so that savage humans can get along with one another.

bonuses.leadin: This man postulated that people behave the way they do because of repressed childhood feelings. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of trauma in which blood supply is insufficient to meet a tissue's needs. Necrosis caused by this type of injury is called infarction.
In patients suffering from ischemia, this interval measured on an EKG trace is often abnormally long. It represents the electrical polarization and depolarization of the right and left ventricles.

Administration of this neurotransmitter results in abnormal lengthening of the QT interval in patients suffering from Long QT syndrome. Produced by the chromaffin cells of adrenal glands, it stimulates the fight-or-flight response of the sympathetic nervous system.

bonuses.leadin: The damage caused by this type of trauma is due to hypoxia, buildup of metabolic waste, and scarcity of metabolic substrates. For 10 points:

parts.text: Name this jazz trumpeter who included "So What" and "Freddie Freeloader" on Kind of Blue.
Davis was an early proponent of this genre of jazz more relaxed than bebop. Jerry Mulligan and John Lewis arranged several standards for a Davis album titled for the "birth" of this style.
One of the biggest influences on Birth of the Cool was this pianist, whose namesake orchestra included Danny Polo on clarinet. He composed the jazz standards "Snowfall" and "I Wish I Had You".

bonuses.leadin: With Gil Evans, this man arranged Joaquin Rodrigo's Concierto de Aranjuez to open his album Sketches of Spain. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Nixtamalization involves dipping this crop into an alkaline solution in order to remove its non-nutritious husk. Barbara McClintock first discovered transposons while studying this model organism.

Nixtamalization's health benefits include freeing up this vitamin from its bound state on corn. This vitamin's amide is a precursor to NAD, and a deficiency of it causes a disease characterized by the "three d's."

Nixtamalization (nix-tuh-mall-ih-zay-shun) also removes these fungi-based carcinogens from the husk of corn. The most potent of these carcinogens, its B1 form, is produced by Aspergillus flavus, (ass-per-JILL-us FLAY-vus) which these toxins are named after.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the process of nixtamalization (nix-tuh-mall-ih-zay-shun). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this work in which Adam and Eve are expelled from the Garden of Eden despite the warnings of Raphael.
This author of Paradise Lost wrote the poem "Lycidas" after the drowning of a friend as well as a work about the blind title character, Samson Agonistes.
This anti-censorship pamphlet by Milton takes its name from a speech by Isocrates and argues against "the discouragement of all learning" by the Licensing Act of 1643.

bonuses.leadin: This epic poem sees Lucifer and his followers cast into hell, where they build the palace Pandemonium. For 10 points each:
